# Phase 3 — Stage-2 + integration

Per-step development log (CLAUDE.md §2.4). One stanza is appended after every
step's commit; this file renders to `docs/dev-log/phase3_<YYYY-MM-DD>.pdf` at
the phase-exit gate.

Phase-3 goal (imp.md): the RiNALMo Stage-2 re-ranker plus aux heads, the
end-to-end two-stage system, and calibration — with the phase's gated statistic
being the **GATE-2 first half**, in-distribution ECE ≤ 0.05 on the
**pre-prior-shift** temperature-scaled posterior (PRD §12; ADR-0005). Phase 2
shipped a segmenter and one passing method gate (GATE-4); it shipped no
calibrated output. Nothing in this phase may be quoted as a discovery result.

## Step P3-01 — 2026-07-31: assemble the Stage-2 supervised dataset + RNA tokenizer adapter

**Inputs.** `data/processed/master_clean_v0.parquet` (DVC, 23,535 records),
`data/processed/labels/labels_v0.parquet` (DVC; the P0-20 per-nt `label_string`
plus the §8 aux labels), the git-LFS `data/processed/splits/split_assignments.parquet`
(ADR-0004 D7, 25,913 rows) and `data/processed/negatives/decoys_v0.parquet`
(DVC, 7,008 §9.1 static decoys). LOCAL, ~8 s, no GPU and no network.

**Process.** `src/tbox_finder/stage2/dataset.py` (rule
`workflow/rules/stage2.smk::stage2_dataset`) emits one row per RNA sequence
Stage 2 will ever score — every positive plus every unmasked decoy — carrying
the binary label, the per-nucleotide boundary target, the §8 aux targets, a
dot-bracket pairing target for the P3-05 structure-consistency loss, and the
ADR-0004 fold/parentage columns. Three choices are load-bearing.

*(i) Sequence-only, flank 0 nt for both classes.* PRD §6 hands Stage 2 a
"locus ± flank", but the named P3-01 inputs supply real genomic flank for
positives only (P2-00's `context_v0`); the four decoy pools are generated,
Rfam-sourced or shuffled and have none. A positives-only flank makes "is
embedded in real genomic context" a perfectly separable shortcut for the binary
head — the §5 circularity failure the project exists to avoid — so `flank_nt` is
a pinned parameter, recorded per row and in provenance, and v0 pins it to **0
for both classes**; a non-zero value is refused by the builder until a matching
flank exists for every pool. Structure appears **only** as a target column, never
an input channel (PRD §6).

*(ii) Folds inherited, never invented.* Each row records `fold_basis` ∈
{`corpus_record`, `parent_record`, `decoy_pool_random`}. A positive copies every
scheme column from its own split-table row. A dinucleotide-shuffled decoy
**inherits its parent's fold across every scheme** — ADR-0004 D7's
variant→parent→fold rule applied to the negative side — and is refused
fail-closed if its parent is absent. The 5,007 decoys with no corpus parent
(generated GC-matched background, Rfam structured RNAs, tboxevo leader decoys)
belong to no cluster and no clade, so no leave-clade-out holdout unit can contain
them; they are handled the way **ADR-0004 D4** handles taxonomy-incomplete
positives — kept **only in the random split**, every clade-scheme column left
null, `clade_holdout_eligible` False — with a deterministic keyed-hash
`fold_random` (seed 20260731, order-independent). `nested_train` is left **null**
for them rather than set True: whether a parentless decoy may enter the nested
training fold is a P3-03 sampling policy, and a `True` here would be a policy
decision disguised as a data field. **This convention is a reading of ADR-0004
D4/D7, not a pinned decision** — flagged for sign-off at the P3-exit gate, since
P3-02's calibration carve inherits it.

*(iii) The pairing target is projected and measured, not assumed.* TBDB's
`Structure` (WUSS) is aligned to `Sequence`, the gapped cmalign row, **not** to
the genomic `FASTA_sequence` locus (median 238 vs 281 nt; co-extensive with each
other on 99.996 % of records but with the locus on 0.5 %). The builder validates
the alignment row, strips gaps, and requires the gap-stripped sequence to occur
**exactly once** in the locus before mapping the pairs through that offset.
Measured over the full corpus: **18,269 / 23,535 (77.62 %)** anchor, with **zero**
no-hit and **zero** multi-hit rows — every clean-alphabet row anchors uniquely,
which is a strong internal consistency check on the projection rather than a
tuned threshold. The other 5,266 render unaligned inserts as `~` / `[n]` / `*`
with the nucleotides **elided** (a lossy view: after sanitising the junk glyphs,
4,590 of 5,259 still have no locus match at all — measured, not assumed), so they
carry `pairing_status = "unanchorable_alignment"` and a **null** target. No
approximate or re-folded structure is substituted (CLAUDE.md §10.3).

A first implementation *rejected* any record whose consensus structure paired
into a column this member had deleted; that discarded 8,634 further records.
Measurement showed the rule was wrong: `Structure` is a consensus line, and only
**20,854 of 850,029 pairs (2.5 %)** have a deleted partner (per-row median
fraction 0.000, max 0.426). Such a pair is not formed in this sequence, so it is
now **dropped and counted** (`n_pairs_dropped_gap`), never re-based onto a
neighbouring nucleotide and never grounds for discarding the row's other 97.5 %
of real pairs. Dropping pairs from a nested set leaves it nested.

**The tokenizer adapter** (`src/tbox_finder/stage2/tokenizer.py`) pins RiNALMo's
28-token alphabet in **pure Python** so the build runs in `envs/data.yml`
alongside every other data-layer rule: `multimolecule` exists only in
`envs/ml-rna.yml` (the ADR-0002 A4 env split) and pulls `deepspeed` at import.
The context bound is **derived, not copied** — `RiNALMoConfig.max_position_embeddings`
is 1024 at the pinned revision and `RnaTokenizer` wraps the sequence in
`<cls>`/`<eos>`, giving PRD §10.2's 1022. Behaviour was read off the live
tokenizer, not assumed: input is upper-cased, `T`→`U`, the 15 IUPAC codes plus
`- . * | ? X I N` are in-vocabulary, and anything else becomes `<unk>` rather
than being dropped, so token length always equals sequence length and the
per-nucleotide target stays index-aligned.

**Outputs.** `data/processed/stage2_dataset.parquet` (DVC, **30,542 rows** ×
34 columns = 23,535 positives + 7,007 decoys; 1 union-prior-masked decoy
excluded) + `stage2_dataset.provenance.json` +
`data/processed/audits/stage2_dataset_report.json`. Artifact digest
`03263354175c0c3db19cd4262b8aff1bbe3ab0f160f30b13774973bec27af764`; longest row
550 nt / 552 tokens (well inside 1024). Fold basis: 23,535 `corpus_record`,
2,000 `parent_record`, 5,007 `decoy_pool_random`. Pairing: 18,269 anchored /
5,266 unanchorable / 7,007 not-applicable; 829,175 base pairs emitted, 20,854
consensus pairs dropped on a deleted partner across 8,634 rows, and **no**
anchored row ends with zero pairs.

**Validation.** Gate **PASS**. Unit + golden green (54 passed / 2 skipped in
`tbox-data`; the 2 skips are the `multimolecule` parity legs, which run **23
passed / 0 skipped** in `tbox-ml-rna`). Tokenizer round-trip
`decode(encode(s)) == s` exact on all 100 real T-box loci of the committed
ingest slice and on the hand-authored alphabet fixture; the pinned vocabulary is
asserted **equal to the live `RnaTokenizer`** at the ADR-0002 A9 revision
`2a71f6f9…`, and the pinned digest is re-derived stdlib-only so a hand-edit
fails in CI even where parity skips. Every row carries a non-null `fold_random`,
`parent_record_id` and a `fold_basis` in the closed set; max tokens 552 ≤ 1022.
`ruff check` + `black --check` clean; `snakemake --lint` "workflow is in a good
condition" and `snakemake -n` parses.

*No pytest exists in any local env, so the suites were executed with a
stdlib pytest shim (`raises`/`match`, `importorskip`, `parametrize`) in both
`tbox-data` and `tbox-ml-rna`; CI runs the real pytest.* **Seven sabotage bites**
were run with `__pycache__` cleared and each restore proved by `cmp` (these files
are new, so `git checkout --` would be a silent no-op): wrong split row for a
derived decoy → `test_derived_decoy_inherits_every_scheme_value_from_its_parent`
(+ golden); gap-partner pair re-based instead of dropped →
`test_projection_drops_a_pair_whose_partner_is_a_deleted_column` (+ golden);
ambiguous anchor takes the first hit → `test_projection_refuses_an_ambiguous_anchor`;
invented clade units on a parentless decoy →
`test_parentless_decoys_are_random_only_and_invent_no_clade` (+ golden); a
vocabulary id edited → `test_vocab_digest_is_pinned` (+3); the T→U transcription
removed → 14 tests incl. the golden. A seventh bite edited a vocabulary id **and
recomputed the pinned digest**, so the CI-side guards pass — it is caught only by
`test_pinned_vocab_matches_live_tokenizer` in `tbox-ml-rna`, proving that leg is
not vacuous.

**Decisions.** (a) `flank_nt = 0` for both classes, refused otherwise — a
symmetry requirement, not a convenience (PRD §5/§6). (b) Parentless decoys are
random-split-only with null clade columns and a null `nested_train` — the
ADR-0004 D4 pattern extended to a class D4 does not name; **owed sign-off at the
P3-exit gate**, cross-ref ADR-0004 D4/D7. (c) The build runs in the `data` env
via a pinned-vocabulary adapter rather than in `ml-rna`, keeping the golden test
CI-runnable; cross-ref ADR-0002 A4/A8/A9. (d) The golden fixture runs with
`require_full_join=False` because 6 of the 100 ingest-fixture records predate the
corpus de-duplication and have no split row; the refused counts (6 records, and
the 4 dinucleotide decoys parented on them) are **asserted**, so the relaxation
is pinned rather than silent — and it makes ADR-0004 D7's fail-closed rule fire
on real data inside the golden. (e) The imp.md gate names "the 9-PDB +
hand-checked fixture" for the round-trip, but those P0-21 fixtures record element
extents and window lengths, **not sequences**; they are used for what they can
assert (the token axis stays index-aligned with the per-nucleotide label axis at
exactly those 11 window lengths) and the round-trip itself runs over real T-box
loci. (f) README/`paper/manuscript.qmd` are **not** touched: this step lands no
analysis result and the repo batches both at the phase-exit gate (the P2
precedent).

**Review round 1 (CodeRabbit, PR #93) — 3 findings, 2 applied, 1 skipped with
reason.** *(major, applied)* The uniqueness check used `str.count`, which counts
**non-overlapping** occurrences — `"AAA".count("AA") == 1` — so a genuinely
ambiguous probe could be reported unique and the structure silently placed at the
first offset, the exact mis-placement the rule exists to prevent. Replaced with an
overlap-aware scan. Re-measured on the full corpus before and after: **0 of 23,535
records differ between the two counts**, anchored stays 18,269 and the artifact
digest is byte-identical — a latent hole closed, not a number moved.
*(minor, applied)* `parent_record_id` was built with `str(cell)`, which turns a
null into the present-looking `"None"` (pandas 2) / `"nan"` (pandas 3) and would
sail past the null gate as a fabricated parent link; now `_text`, so a null
reaches the gate. *(major, skipped with reason)* The reviewer asked for the four
source artifacts to be declared as Snakemake `input:`. Tested rather than argued:
adding them (a) **fails `snakemake --lint`** with "Param … is a prefix of input or
output file but hardcoded" — the CI-blocking rule — and (b) makes
`snakemake -n stage2_dataset` schedule a **6-job rebuild** of
`extract_split_sequences` → `align_split_positives` → `cluster_and_split` →
`classII_recovery_set` → `split_assignment_table`, i.e. it would **regenerate the
committed ADR-0004 split table** the no-leakage CI gate is anchored on. The
DVC/git-LFS-tracked inputs stay out of the DAG, which is the documented house
convention (`data.smk::derive_labels`). Restored byte-identical (`cmp`); with the
rule as shipped, `snakemake -n stage2_dataset` says "Nothing to be done".
Both applied fixes carry a new test and were sabotage-verified: reverting the
overlap scan fails only
`test_projection_refuses_an_OVERLAPPING_ambiguous_anchor`, reverting `_text` fails
only `test_a_null_parent_link_is_refused_not_stringified`.

**Review round 2 (CodeRabbit, PR #93) — 2 minor findings, both applied.**
`decode`/`id_to_token` cast with `int()`, and `int(6.9)` is `6`, so a corrupted
float id would silently decode as the nucleotide at 6 — the opposite of the
docstring's "an id outside the vocabulary is an error, not a silent `<unk>`".
Now `operator.index`, which still accepts the NumPy integers a parquet round-trip
yields (asserted) and refuses floats/strings/`None`; new test
`test_decode_refuses_a_non_integer_id`, sabotage-verified (reverting to `int()`
fails that test alone). The second finding was prose: the round-1 comment said
"scan every start position" while the code does two `find`s — corrected to
describe the second search from `offset + 1`, no code change. 57 passed / 2
skipped in `tbox-data`; 24 passed / 0 skipped in `tbox-ml-rna`.

**Commit.** Branch `p3-01-stage2-dataset`, PR #93 (3 commits: the step + two
review rounds) — the **squash SHA on `main` is not yet known** and must be
reconciled at the P3-exit gate by deriving it
(`git show <sha> -- analyses/phase3_log.qmd | grep '^+## Step'`), never copied
from notes.

## Step P3-02 — 2026-08-01: carve the disjoint calibration split (cluster-respecting) + re-run no-leakage

**Inputs.** The committed git-LFS `data/processed/splits/split_assignments.parquet`
(ADR-0004 D7, 25,913 rows, sha256 `6388ba19…`), its DVC-interim source, and
`data/processed/stage2_dataset.parquet` (P3-01, 30,542 rows, digest `03263354…`).
LOCAL, ~30 s, no GPU and no network.

**Process.** ADR-0005 **D11** pins the recalibration stack as *train → temperature-scale
on a disjoint calibration split → prior-shift*, but ADR-0004's fold vocabulary had **no
calibration fold**: A11 (P2-13) recorded the absence, fitted its non-gated Stage-1 `T` on
a seeded half of the P2-06a `selection_val` rung as a stopgap, and named P3-02 as the step
that carves the real one. This step signs **ADR-0004 A7** and builds it. `calib` is drawn
by `splits.calib_cluster_ids` from the pool
`source == "corpus" ∧ nested_train ∧ fold_random == "train" ∧ cluster ∉ selection_val`
(**5,034 records / 2,526 clusters**), and written by `splits.carve_calibration_split`
inside `build_split_table` — *before* `append_variant_rows`, which is what makes variant
`calib` inheritance structural rather than conventional.

Three choices are load-bearing.

*(i) The `fold_random == "train"` conjunct does the disjointness structurally.* `fold_random`
is whole-cluster assigned (measured: **0** clusters span >1 non-null value), so excluding
the value excludes the cluster. It also removes ADR-0004 **A6**'s `gate4_eval` population
(1,204 records / 1,031 clusters) in full — measured, the pool is the same 5,034 records
with or without a separate `gate4_eval` exclusion, so the emptiness of that intersection is
a *consequence* of the rule, asserted rather than assumed. The pool is disjoint from **both**
candidate Stage-2 in-distribution test populations, so it does not pre-empt P3-03's
train-eligibility policy.

*(ii) The draw is genus-stratified because the uniform one is not representative — measured.*
The eligible pool is **98.5 % Firmicutes / 56.7 % Bacillales**, and only **2 of its 25
orders** carry ≥ 20 records. The uniform whole-cluster draw used for `selection_val` reaches
**6 orders / 4 phyla** at fraction 0.10; genus stratification reaches **23 orders / 13
phyla** (859 records / 431 clusters, realised fraction **17.1 %** — a stratum cannot
subdivide a whole cluster). Genus is not a new device: scheme A is itself
"random (**genus-stratified**)" (PRD §9.2), so `calib` is drawn the way the split it must
mirror was drawn. Stage-2 training loses those 859 of 5,034 eligible positives — the
intrinsic price of D11's word *disjoint*.

*(iii) The negative side is prevalence-matched, because a binary head cannot be calibrated
on a positives-only fold.* The committed table has **no negative rows** at all (the A4/b2
blind spot), so P3-01 had left open — explicitly, flagged for this step — whether a
parentless decoy may enter `calib`. Inherit-only gives 64 negatives → prevalence **0.931**
against the in-distribution test split's **0.7727**; admitting every train-fold parentless
decoy gives **0.174**. A7.4 therefore admits parentless decoys from the **train portion
only**, at `DECOY_CALIB_RATE = 0.0469`, by a keyed hash under a distinct `":calib:"` domain
prefix — a *second* draw rather than a 4-way widening of `decoy_fold`, because
re-partitioning the existing 0.80/0.10/0.10 mass would move decoys across the train/val/test
boundary and silently change a partition P3-01 already committed. `nested_train` stays
**null** for them: A7 says what the calibration *fit* may see, and resolves nothing about
P3-03's sampling policy.

**A fork this step exposed.** `data/window_dataset.py` carried its own hand-typed
`FOLD_SCHEME_COLUMNS` commented *"the six … (splits.FOLD_SCHEME_COLUMNS)"*. Adding `calib`
upstream put it one column behind and **nothing failed**. Stage 1 is right not to carry a
Stage-2 calibration flag — widening `CorpusRecord.folds` would change
`negatives.NEGATIVE_FOLDS`, every `zip(…, strict=True)` over the pair, and every committed
Stage-1 report shape — so the tuple is now **derived** as
`splits.FOLD_SCHEME_COLUMNS − STAGE2_ONLY_FOLD_COLUMNS`, leaving its content and order
identical while making the omission a named decision
([[promote-dont-duplicate-is-a-correctness-rule]]).

**Outputs.** Regenerated `data/processed/splits/split_assignments.parquet` (git-LFS,
25,913 × **21** columns, sha256 `d51252ee…`, `extra.table_schema_version` **1.1**) with its
provenance `extra.calib` block (seed 20260801, fraction 0.10, 5,034 eligible → **859
records / 431 clusters / 23 orders / 13 phyla**, realised 0.17064); regenerated
`data/processed/stage2_dataset.parquet` (DVC, md5 `23f412dc…`, digest `c5a2c251…`,
30,542 × **35** columns) + `stage2_dataset_report.json → calib`.

**Validation.** Gate **PASS**. The full-corpus no-leakage suite is green — **57 passed /
0 failed** (49 before this step) with `TBOX_REQUIRE_NO_LEAKAGE=1`, including the new
`test_scheme_calibration_carve_is_disjoint_and_rederivable`. On the real partition:
calib ∩ {val, test} = **0**, ∩ `selection_val` = **0**, ∩ `gate4_eval` = **0**, ∩ designated
LOO holdout = **0**, ∩ clade-crossing = **0**, clusters straddling calib/training = **0**.
The 22 corpus cluster-mates left outside `calib` are **all** `nested_role == "dropped"` and
**0** are `nested_train`, so nothing in the training stream is orphaned.

The CI clause never reads the committed boolean back: it **re-derives** the carve from
`cluster_id`/`nested_train`/`fold_random`/`resolved_genus` + the pinned seed and asserts
**set identity** ([[gate-clauses-need-re-derivation]]). Verified by sabotage on the real
table, not by reading — seven targeted mutations (clear one bit, admit one extra record,
move a calib record to `test`, split a calib cluster, blank the column, carve the whole
pool, admit a `selection_val` record), each biting the intended clause;
`loosening_admits_the_refused` is non-vacuous the other way, TRUE at baseline because
dropping the `fold_random == "train"` conjunct grows the pool **5,034 → 6,366**.
`disjoint_from_selection_val` / `disjoint_from_gate4_eval` are structurally implied by the
pool definition and are retained as guards on a future pool change, not as independent
evidence — stated rather than counted as bite.

Other suites: `test_split_table_schema` 33 (was 27), `test_stage2_dataset` 27 (was 24),
`test_window_dataset` 76 (was 75), golden 3, `test_negatives` 36, `test_split_assignment`
11 — all 0 failed against a **matched control sweep of the same runner on `main`**, which
is how the 11 apparent new "skips" were traced to DVC artifacts absent in a fresh worktree
rather than to this change. `ruff check` + `black --check` clean at the CI-pinned versions
(0.15.15 / 25.11.0); `snakemake --lint` "workflow is in a good condition"; `snakemake -n`
parses. Both artifacts were regenerated **after** the `black` reformat and reproduce
byte-identical digests, so the shipped bytes are the measured ones
([[verify-the-line-you-ship]]).

**The one number that did not land on target, reported not tuned.** The realised
calibration set is **859 positives / 230 negatives = prevalence 0.7888** against the test
split's **0.7727** — **+1.6 pp**. The keyed hash drew 168 parentless decoys where the rate's
expectation is 188.9 (−1.6 σ), and 62 rather than 64 inherited, two eligible shuffles being
union-prior-masked out. `DECOY_CALIB_RATE` is **not** re-tuned to close the gap: the rate is
the pinned quantity and the prevalence is a measurement (CLAUDE.md §10.3). The rejected
inherit-only rule sits 15.4 pp off. Both numbers ship as report constants so a drift is
visible rather than inferred.

**Disclosed limitation.** `calib` is carved from inside `nested_train`, so its clade support
is narrower than the test split's **by construction**: 23 orders / 13 phyla vs the test
split's 48 orders / 12 phyla (the extra orders are the held-out clades `nested_train`
excludes — they *cannot* appear in a training-fold carve). At phylum level the two are close
(Firmicutes 0.962 vs 0.941); at order level calib is Bacillales 0.491 / Clostridiales 0.469
vs test 0.364 / 0.278. This is a calibration-transfer caveat for the P3-10 GATE-2 artifact
to carry, **not** corrected by reweighting, which would be an unpinned estimator.

**Decisions.** **ADR-0004 A7** drafted, measured, and **signed** (bioedca, 2026-08-01,
AskUserQuestion; CLAUDE.md §7 item 2) — all three forks taken as drafted: prevalence-matched
negatives, fraction 0.10, and a committed column plus CI re-derivation rather than a derived
predicate. A7 discharges ADR-0005 **A11**'s disclosure (iii): GATE-2's `T` is re-fitted here,
and **no `T` from P2-13 is inherited**. `imp.md` P3-02 named
`src/tbox_finder/data/splits.py::carve_calibration_split`; there is no such module and the
entry point landed in `src/tbox_finder/splits.py` — roadmap path drift, corrected there.

**Review round 1 (CodeRabbit CLI, PR #94) — 2 findings, both real defects, both fixed.**
*(a)* `CALIB_STRATUM_COLUMN` was **decorative**: it is a pinned constant *and* the value
the provenance sidecar reports as `calib.stratum_column`, but the carve read
`table["resolved_genus"]` by name. Changing the constant would have left the committed
provenance claiming a stratification the carve never performed — a fabricated provenance
value (§10.3) with nothing failing. Every caller now selects the column through the
constant; verified load-bearing by execution (the real carve moves **859 → 526** records
when it is pointed at `resolved_order`). *(b)* The calib guard re-derived with the
**module-default** seed while `build_dataset` threads a caller's `decoy_fold_seed` into
`decoy_calib` — so any non-default seed compared the built rows against a different hash:
the guard would fire on a correct build and could never fire on a wrong one. The seed is
threaded through, and the guard now re-derives over **every** parentless row instead of
filtering to `calib=True` first, so a decoy wrongly left *out* — the count-preserving
direction — is caught too.

**Two of my own tests were structurally blind, and sabotage is what said so.** The first
seed test used `DECOY_FOLD_SEED + 1`; the fixture has only two parentless decoys and at
rate 0.0469 almost every seed leaves both False, so it **passed with the fix reverted**. It
now uses a *searched* seed (20260737) that provably disagrees with the default and asserts
that disagreement explicitly, so it cannot go vacuous again. The stratum test had the
mirror problem: the unit fixture carried one genus per order, so genus- and
order-stratification coincided (both → 2) and the test passed with the constant still
decorative; the fixture now holds two genera inside one order (genus → 3, order → 2)
([[vacuous-test-perturbations]], [[degenerate-fixture-generators]]).

**Review round 2 (CodeRabbit CLI) — 2 findings, both applied; one real, one defensive.**
*(a)* **Real:** `test_decoy_calib_is_independent_of_the_fold_draw` asserted independence
through a rate band, but the very bug it names — implementing `calib` as the low tail of
the *same* unit interval `decoy_fold` partitions — yields **0.0536** among train-fold
decoys (`DECOY_CALIB_RATE / 0.80`), which sits inside any band loose enough to survive
binomial noise. Measured, then replaced with an assertion **by identity** against the
shared-domain set; sabotage-verified (collapsing the hash domain now fails that test).
*(b)* **Defensive:** `_calib_provenance` counted `calib` over all rows while
`n_eligible_records` counted corpus rows only. Measured on the committed table this is a
**no-op** — 0 non-corpus calib rows, and `_assert_calib_disjoint` refuses them before the
provenance is written — but numerator and denominator now range over the same population,
so a `realised_fraction` cannot go wrong if that assertion is ever reordered or relaxed.

## Step P3-03 — 2026-08-02: build the RiNALMo-giga Stage-2 multi-head model (sequence-only)

**Inputs.** The pinned `multimolecule/rinalmo-giga` encoder @ revision
`2a71f6f98fb4…` (ADR-0002 D2/D5/A9); `src/tbox_finder/train/lora_harness.py` (the P1-15
LoRA entry, which owns the PRD §10.3 pins); `data/processed/stage2_dataset.parquet`
(P3-02-regenerated, digest `c5a2c251…`, 30,542 rows) read once to derive two head
vocabularies; `labels.CLASS_ORDER`, `ingest.TYPE_TO_CLASS`, and
`tests/fixtures/pdb_element_extents/`. LOCAL, CPU only — no GPU, no SLURM, no network
beyond the already-cached checkpoint.

**Process.** `src/tbox_finder/stage2/model.py::Stage2Model` puts the four PRD §10.2 heads
on the encoder: (a) binary T-box `(B,)`, (b) per-base boundary refinement `(B, L, 8)`,
(c) regulatory mode `(B, 2)`, (d) the G-D auxiliary triple — specifier codon `(B, 64)`,
cognate amino acid `(B, 20)`, tRNA family `(B, 61)`. Head (b) **reuses**
`models.seg_head.SegmentationHead` rather than reimplementing an 8-class per-nt head, so
Stage 1 and Stage 2 cannot drift apart on the ADR-0004 D1 vocabulary. The backbone-free
surface (`heads_from_hidden`) mirrors `Stage1Segmenter`'s and is what the CPU unit tier
drives, so no test needs the 2.5 GB checkout.

Four things are load-bearing.

*(i) No ADR or the PRD pins a single head cardinality*, so none is typed here.
`stage2/heads.py` (torch-free, hence CI-locked) derives head (b) from
`labels.CLASS_ORDER`, head (c) from the keys of `ingest.TYPE_TO_CLASS`, and head (d1) by
enumerating `product("ACGU", 3)` — all 64 triplets are attested in the corpus, so the
axis is the genetic code, not an over-wide guess. The cognate-amino-acid and tRNA-family
axes are TBDB *spellings* with no canonical source, so `derive_head_spec` reads them off
the **whole** committed dataset and the result is committed as
`src/tbox_finder/stage2/head_vocab.json` with provenance. Per-caller derivation was
rejected: a vocabulary read from the train fold alone gives the test fold classes the
head has no logit for.

*(ii) The sequence-only prohibition is structural, not conventional.* PRD §10.2 —
"RiNALMo ingests **sequence only** (no structure-input channel)" — is enforced by
`forward(*, input_ids, attention_mask)` declaring no `**kwargs`, so a dot-bracket string
is a `TypeError` at the call site. The test that locks this reads the shipped file with
`ast` instead of importing it: `model.py` imports `torch` at module top, so an
import-based check could only run where torch exists, i.e. never in CI — the one place
the prohibition is checked on every push.

*(iii) LoRA wraps the encoder; the heads sit outside it.* `build_stage2_model` calls
`lora_harness.build_peft_model` on the backbone **alone**, then attaches the heads. Both
halves matter: `target_modules="all-linear"` adapts every `nn.Linear` it can reach, so
heads inside the wrapper would be LoRA-adapted rather than trained; and
`build_peft_model`'s frozen-base clause ("no trainable parameter lacking `lora_` in its
name") would be tripped by the heads and stop meaning anything. The split is
**re-measured** off the assembled model into `info["stage2_heads"]`, not asserted.

*(iv) The token axis is not the nucleotide axis.* `RnaTokenizer` wraps every sequence in
`<cls> … <eos>`, so the encoder emits `L + 2` positions while `label_string` has `L`.
`strip_special_tokens` reproduces `multimolecule`'s own `remove_special_tokens` contract
(drop position 0, zero each row's EOS at its own last valid index, drop the trailing
column), which leaves every row's nucleotides at indices `0 … L_i-1` with padding zeroed
— index-aligned to that row's label string, in a ragged batch, with no gather.

**A data defect the derivation surfaced.** The first derived tRNA-family vocabulary had
**62** entries, one of them the literal `"None (UCA)"`. All **9** rows carrying it have a
blank `cognate_aa` and a `UGA` (opal) specifier: TBDB composes the family as
`f"{amino_acid} ({anticodon})"`, so a record with no amino acid renders its own absence
as text. It survives every missing check — `masking.is_missing` sees a well-formed string
— and would have given head (d3) a logit for a tRNA family that does not exist.
`is_admissible_label` now refuses whole-cell null tokens on every axis and a null
amino-acid component on the family axis, at **both** the vocabulary-building and the
encoding site so the two cannot disagree. The axis is **61**, and the cross-check that
makes it verifiable is that `trna_family` and `cognate_aa` now encode the *same*
**22,932** rows — as they must, one being composed from the other.

**Outputs.** `src/tbox_finder/stage2/heads.py` · `src/tbox_finder/stage2/model.py` ·
`src/tbox_finder/stage2/head_vocab.json` (head widths 8 / 2 / 64 / 20 / 61, source digest
`c5a2c251…`) · `tests/unit/test_stage2_heads.py` · `tests/unit/test_stage2_model.py` ·
the `stage2/__init__.py` docstring carve-out for the one module that may import torch at
top level. No DVC artifact, no checkpoint, no W&B run — this step trains nothing.

**Validation.** **79 passed / 0 failed** in `tbox-ml-rna`; **57 passed / 22 skipped /
0 failed** in a torch-free env (the CI tier). No local env carries both pytest and torch,
so the shipped test bytes were executed through a minimal pytest shim; CI runs the real
pytest. **Four source sabotages, each RED then restored byte-identical (sha256-verified,
`python -B`):** dropping the EOS removal → 8 RED incl.
`test_the_eos_token_is_removed_not_merely_shifted`; deleting the tRNA null-amino-acid
clause → 4 RED; making an out-of-vocabulary value encode to class 0 instead of masking →
2 RED; adding `**kwargs` to `forward` → `test_forward_declares_no_var_kwargs` RED **in
the bare tier**, which is the tier that has to catch it. **Step-local §8.5 gate on the
real pretrained checkpoint** (the imp.md gate clause, too heavy for CI):
`LoraConfig(r=16, α=32, dropout=0.05, target_modules="all-linear")` loads on
rinalmo-giga @ `2a71f6f9…` and adapts **231 of 231** eligible `nn.Linear`
(`all_linear_fully_covered = true`, PEFT suffix-minimises the selector to six leaf names
— not a count); `base_frozen = true` with **0** base trainable params; trainable
**12,840,432 / 662,079,483 = 1.9394 %**; the six heads are **199,836** params, **none**
LoRA-adapted and **all** trainable; `d_model = 1280` measured off the backbone, not
defaulted; a CPU forward on two real-length RNAs gives every head its correct shape, all
finite, with `nucleotide_mask` sums `[34, 28]` equal to the input sequence lengths. The
load report's `lm_head.*` UNEXPECTED keys are the pretraining MLM head, correctly not
loaded into the encoder-only `RiNALMoModel`. `ruff check` + `black --check` clean at the CI-pinned versions (ruff 0.15.15, black 25.11.0).

**Decisions.** No new ADR and no amendment: ADR-0002 D5/A9 already pin the checkpoint and
PRD §10.3 already pins the LoRA scalars, and this step re-uses both rather than restating
either — the head cardinalities the documents leave open are *derived and committed*, not
pinned by fiat. Two defaults are this step's own and are flagged for P3-06 rather than
frozen: sequence-level pooling is a **masked mean over nucleotide positions** (the
checkpoint has no pooler and `load_rinalmo_backbone` passes `add_pooling_layer=False`, so
there is no pretrained `<cls>` summary to read), and head (b) defaults to `use_crf=False`
with the CRF exposed as a constructor knob. §10.1 evidence gate N/A — this step asserts no
biological fact; the one factual claim it makes (`"None (UCA)"` is a rendered absence) is
measured off the committed corpus, not from the literature. Cross-refs: ADR-0004 D1
(head (b)'s class order), ADR-0005 D16 (the aux-weighting method P3-04 will apply to
these heads), ADR-0002 A2 K1 (attention backend selected from measured evidence, never a
free knob).

yet known** and must be reconciled at the P3-exit gate by deriving it
(`git show <sha> -- analyses/phase3_log.qmd | grep '^+## Step'`), never copied from notes.

## Step P3-04 — 2026-08-02: the multi-task aux-loss with the ADR-0005 D16 pinned weighting method

**Inputs.** The six `Stage2Model.forward` head outputs plus the `nucleotide_mask` P3-03
returns for exactly this purpose (`stage2/model.py::OUTPUT_KEYS`); `stage2/heads.py`'s
`IGNORE_INDEX` and the committed `head_vocab.json` widths 8 / 2 / 64 / 20 / 61;
`train/objective.py::focal_cross_entropy` and its inverse-frequency weight arithmetic.
LOCAL, CPU only — no GPU, no SLURM, no checkpoint, no DVC artifact.

**Process.** `src/tbox_finder/stage2/losses.py::multitask_loss` combines six masked terms —
(a) binary, (b) per-nucleotide boundary, (c) regulatory mode, (d1–d3) the G-D auxiliaries —
under ADR-0005 D16's pinned method, with `MultitaskLoss` as the stateful wrapper that
derives class weights from measured counts and `Stage2LossConfig` as the frozen, validated
config. `conf/loss/stage2.yaml` is a new Hydra group carrying every field as a literal key
and wired into `conf/train/lora_stage2.yaml`, so the PRD §11 sweep axis is
`loss.aux_weight=…` exactly as the learning-rate axis is `optim.lr=…`.

Five choices are load-bearing.

**(1) Nothing is forked; the binary head is restated rather than reimplemented.** Every
term routes through the P2-02 `focal_cross_entropy`, including head (a), whose single
logit `z` is expressed as the pair `[0, z]` — softmax over which is `[1-σ(z), σ(z)]`, so
cross-entropy against a `{0,1}` target *is* `binary_cross_entropy_with_logits`, with the
same `σ(z) − y` gradient (the fabricated channel is a `zeros_like` constant and carries
none). A unit test pins that equality against torch's own BCE as an **external** witness,
and a sabotage bite that swaps the two channels turns it RED. The point is not economy: a
separate binary focal loss would be a second place to get the ignore-index handling, the
`Σ w_y` weighted-mean denominator, and P2-02's `clamp_min(eps)` — the fix for the silent
NaN gradient at `0 < γ < 1` — wrong.

**(2) Masked, not dense, with the emptiness made visible.** All 7,007 decoy rows carry no
head-(c)/(d) target at all, so a term must reduce over its supervised elements only.
Measured on the pinned torch 2.7.1, `F.cross_entropy(reduction="mean")` returns **nan**
when every target in a batch is ignored — the shared focal path returns `0.0` instead. But
a silently-vacuous term and a well-behaved one both read as a small number, so every term
reports its own `n_supervised` beside its value and the excluded terms are listed by name
(`skipped_unsupervised`, `included`). The test that pins this also asserts the *witness*:
torch's own path on the same batch **is** nan, so the check is not vacuous.

**(3) D16's "binary head weighted to dominate" is qualitative, and the encoding is
reported rather than self-certified.** It is enforced as `binary_weight ≥ Σ effective aux
weights`, checked at construction (login node, before any GPU time); the weaker per-term
reading (`binary ≥ each aux`) is computed and reported beside it. The two are **not** the
same rule, and the divergence was measured across the sweep range rather than argued: at
the shipped base weights (binary 1.0; boundary 0.3; four record-level heads 0.1 each,
Σ aux = 0.7) they agree for `aux_weight ≤ 1.4286` and again for `> 3.334`, and **disagree
on `aux_weight ∈ (1.4286, 3.334]`** — a window a sweep could plausibly enter. The sum
reading is the one that ships because under the weak one five aux terms at 0.99 out-gradient
a binary at 1.0 while still being called dominated. Raising the cap is an ADR-0005 amendment
(CLAUDE.md §7 item 2), not a config value.

**(4) `aux_weight = 0` is exactly the P3-08 no-aux arm, to the last bit.** It scales all
five non-binary terms and not head (a), so the total reduces to the binary term
(`allclose atol=1e-14`), the aux heads receive no gradient at all, and their unweighted
values are still *reported* — turning the aux heads off stays auditable rather than
becoming invisible. Under the uncertainty method the aux tasks are dropped entirely,
regulariser included, because a task with a live `s_i/2` and no data term opposing it hands
the optimiser a free minimisation that drives that weight to infinity; the same exclusion
therefore applies per batch to any term with no supervision in it.

**(5) Two things are refused rather than quietly done.** A `boundary_crf` argument raises:
`SegmentationHead(use_crf=True)` adds transition parameters a cross-entropy term would leave
with zero gradient, and P3-06 owns that decision (P3-03 flagged it), so a model that looks
trained with a dead CRF is not reachable from here. And an unknown key in `targets` raises,
because a mis-keyed target trains nothing while every loss stays finite and plausible — the
failure mode `label_source` had at P2-11.

D16's **pre-registered alternative** is implemented too, off by default and behind a closed
two-value allow-list: `weighting="uncertainty"` uses the log-variance form
`Σ_i [ exp(−s_i)·L_i + s_i/2 ]` with `s_i = log σ_i²`, i.e. Kendall, Gal & Cipolla's
homoscedastic-uncertainty weighting (arXiv:1705.07115) in the **classification**
parameterisation `σ⁻²L + log σ` — every Stage-2 term here is a cross-entropy, so that is the
applicable coefficient rather than the regression form's extra ½ on the data term
(DOI:10.1002/mp.15870 eq. 4; DOI:10.1049/cmu2.12793 eq. 17, both accessed 2026-08-02; the
`s` parameterisation avoids the `1/σ²` division by zero, DOI:10.1155/2022/6653598 eq. 12).
The learnable log-variances belong to the **caller** (`uncertainty_log_variances`), keeping
this a parameter-free callable the way `Stage1Loss` consumes the head's CRF. Selecting it is
not a method change — D16 names it — but it is recorded in `diagnostics()` so a run using it
is visible.

`train/objective.py` gained one promotion, not a fork: the inverse-frequency arithmetic is
now `inverse_frequency_weights(counts, alpha=…)` over **any** vocabulary (the Stage-2 axes
are 2 / 20 / 61 / 64 wide, not 8), with `class_weights_from_counts` delegating to it and
keeping its CLASS_ORDER-named zero-count message. Verified bit-identical to the
pre-promotion formula over **2,000 random count vectors × α** (0 differences at the bit
level), with `test_objective.py` green as the regression net. `_finite_float` became public
`finite_float` with the private name kept as an alias.

**Validation.** `tests/unit/test_stage2_losses.py`, four tiers: **91 pass / 0 fail** under
`tbox-ml-rna`, and **55 pass / 36 skip** torch-free — the bare run includes the Hydra tier,
which composes the shipped `conf/` tree for real and asserts that *every* dataclass field
has a literal YAML key (the job-669 struct-mode trap), that `loss.aux_weight=0.0` lands,
that a mistyped key is refused, and that the YAML defaults equal the dataclass defaults.
Terms are graded against **external** references (`F.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits`,
`F.cross_entropy`) in fp64 at `atol=1e-12`, never against a recomputation of the
implementation. Gradients flow to all six heads and are exactly zero at ignored targets, at
γ ∈ {0, 0.5, 2} — 0.5 being the regime P2-02's `clamp_min` exists for. Neighbouring suites
re-run green: `test_objective` 92, `test_lora_harness` 107, `test_stage2_heads` 60,
`test_stage2_model` 24, `test_stage2_tokenizer` 24. `ruff@0.15.15` + `black@25.11.0` clean.

**Ten source sabotages, each RED against the named test, each restored byte-identically**
(sha256-verified, `python -B`, `__pycache__` cleared): the binary channel swap; the
dominance rule downgraded to the weak reading; an unsupervised term left in the uncertainty
total; the padded-position test inverted; `aux_weight` applied to the binary term;
two aux terms' vocabulary fields swapped (an **import-time** `RuntimeError` — the pairing
guard runs on load, not only in a test); `n_supervised` reporting the padded element count;
the graph-carrying zero replaced by `torch.zeros(())`; the ½ dropped from the log-variance
regulariser; and `aux_weight` commented out of the YAML.

**One of my own tests was structurally blind and only sabotage said so.** The
padded-position refusal asserted "it raised" — which an *inverted* mask test also satisfies,
since a check that raises on everything raises there too. It now carries its own positive
control (the identical uncorrupted batch must succeed first), and the bite lands on that
test by name.

⚠ No laptop env carries both pytest and torch, so the shipped test bytes were executed
locally through a minimal pytest shim (which expands `parametrize` rather than skipping it);
CI is what confirms collection and skip behaviour under the real runner.

**Decisions.** ADR-0005 D16 is implemented as written — the *method* is unchanged, so no
amendment and no §7 sign-off (imp.md P3-04's `Stops:` makes sign-off conditional on a
method change that only P3-08 could force). Every numeric weight, γ and α is an implementer
default on the PRD §11 swept axis and `diagnostics()["pinned"]` records that split per field
rather than letting a swept default read as a decision.

**Commit.** Branch `p3-04-stage2-losses`, PR pending — the **squash SHA on `main` is not
yet known** and must be reconciled at the P3-exit gate by deriving it
(`git show <sha> -- analyses/phase3_log.qmd | grep '^+## Step'`), never copied from notes.
